sql_server: <replace: SQL Server name, e.g. localhost or MYSERVER\INSTANCE>
database: <replace: name of the database to back up>
sql_username: <optional: SQL login name. Leave empty to use the Windows login of the user running the program>
sql_password: <optional: password for sql_username. Safer: set it in the SQLBACKUP_SQL_PASSWORD environment variable instead>
backup_folder: <replace: folder on this PC for the .bak files, e.g. D:\SqlBackups (use double backslashes). SQL Server must be able to write here>
part_count: <optional: number of .bak files the backup is split into, 1 to 64. Type a number without quotes. Default 30>
s3_prefix: <optional: folder inside the bucket where backups are stored, e.g. prod. Empty = top of the bucket>
aws_region: <replace: AWS Region of your bucket and SNS topic, e.g. us-east-1>
aws_profile: <optional: AWS CLI profile name. Empty = the default profile saved by aws configure>
config_path: <optional: SSM Parameter Store path to read settings from, e.g. /sqlbackup. Empty = use this file only>
sns_topic_arn: <optional: SNS topic ARN for success/failure emails. Empty = no emails>
upload_storage_class: <optional: S3 storage class for new backups. Keep STANDARD (default), or use the same value as cheap_storage_class>
cheap_storage_class: <optional: class older backups are moved to: STANDARD_IA (default), ONEZONE_IA, INTELLIGENT_TIERING, GLACIER_IR, GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE>
cheap_tier_retention_days: <optional: days an older backup is kept after it moves to the cheap class, then deleted. Minimum 30. Default 60>
local_keep_sets: <optional: how many uploaded backups to keep on this PC. 0 = delete them after upload. Default 1>
max_backup_age_days: <optional: for --check only. Sends an alert if the newest backup in S3 is older than this many days. Default 9>
start_mode: <optional: manual = wait for the Start click, auto = start by itself when opened. Default manual>
